source.text: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὸ ἀρνίον μίαν ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ σφραγίδων, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγοντος ὡς φωνῇ βροντῆς· Ἔρχου.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw when opened the Lamb one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying as with a voice of thunder: Come.

en.L: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as with a voice of thunder, "Come!"
en.B: I looked on as the Lamb broke open one of the seven seals. One of the four living creatures cried out with a voice like thunder, and I heard it say, "Come!"
en.R: Then I watched the Lamb open the first of the seven seals. I heard one of the four living creatures shout with a voice like thunder. It said, "Come!"

fr.L: Et je vis quand l’Agneau ouvrit l’un des sept sceaux, et j’entendis l’un des quatre êtres vivants dire, comme d’une voix de tonnerre : « Viens ! »
fr.B: Je regardai l’Agneau briser l’un des sept sceaux. L’un des quatre êtres vivants s’écria d’une voix pareille au tonnerre, et je l’entendis dire : « Viens ! »
fr.R: Ensuite, j’ai vu l’Agneau ouvrir le premier des sept sceaux. J’ai entendu l’un des quatre êtres vivants crier d’une voix forte comme le tonnerre. Il a dit : « Viens ! »

es.L: Y vi cuando el Cordero abrió uno de los siete sellos, y oí a uno de los cuatro seres vivientes que decía, como con voz de trueno: «¡Ven!».
es.B: Vi cómo el Cordero rompía uno de los siete sellos. Uno de los cuatro seres vivientes gritó con una voz como de trueno, y le oí decir: «¡Ven!».
es.R: Luego vi al Cordero abrir el primero de los siete sellos. Oí a uno de los cuatro seres vivientes gritar con una voz como de trueno. Dijo: «¡Ven!».

sw.L: Na niliona Mwanakondoo alipoufungua mmoja wa ile mihuri saba, nikamsikia mmoja wa wale viumbe hai wanne akisema kama kwa sauti ya ngurumo, "Njoo!"
sw.B: Nilitazama Mwanakondoo alipouvunja mmoja wa ile mihuri saba. Mmoja wa wale viumbe hai wanne alipaza sauti kama ngurumo, nikamsikia akisema, "Njoo!"
sw.R: Kisha nikamtazama Mwanakondoo akiufungua muhuri wa kwanza kati ya ile mihuri saba. Nilimsikia mmoja wa wale viumbe hai wanne akipiga kelele kwa sauti kama ngurumo. Alisema, "Njoo!"

vi.L: Và tôi thấy khi Chiên Con mở một trong bảy ấn, và tôi nghe một trong bốn sinh vật nói như tiếng sấm: "Hãy đến!"
vi.B: Tôi nhìn xem khi Chiên Con gỡ ấn thứ nhất trong bảy ấn. Một trong bốn sinh vật kêu lên với tiếng như sấm, và tôi nghe nó nói: "Hãy đến!"
vi.R: Rồi tôi nhìn Chiên Con mở ấn thứ nhất trong bảy ấn. Tôi nghe một trong bốn sinh vật kêu lớn với tiếng như sấm. Nó nói: "Hãy đến!"

ko.L: 그리고 나는 어린양이 일곱 봉인 가운데 하나를 떼실 때에 보았다. 그리고 네 생물 가운데 하나가 천둥 같은 소리로 "오너라!" 하고 말하는 것을 들었다.
ko.B: 나는 어린양이 일곱 봉인 가운데 하나를 떼시는 것을 지켜보았다. 그때 네 생물 가운데 하나가 천둥 같은 소리로 외쳤다. 나는 그가 "오너라!" 하고 말하는 것을 들었다.
ko.R: 그때 나는 어린양이 일곱 봉인 가운데 첫째 봉인을 떼시는 것을 보았다. 나는 네 생물 가운데 하나가 천둥 같은 소리로 외치는 것을 들었다. 그 생물이 말했다. "오너라!"

pt.L: E vi quando o Cordeiro abriu um dos sete selos, e ouvi um dos quatro seres viventes dizendo, como com voz de trovão: "Venha!"
pt.B: Vi quando o Cordeiro rompeu um dos sete selos. Um dos quatro seres viventes gritou com voz de trovão, e eu o ouvi dizer: "Venha!"
pt.R: Então vi o Cordeiro abrir o primeiro dos sete selos. Ouvi um dos quatro seres viventes gritar com uma voz que parecia um trovão. Ele disse: "Venha!"

am.L: በጉም ከሰባቱ ማኅተሞች አንዱን በከፈተ ጊዜ አየሁ፤ ከአራቱም ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት አንዱ እንደ ነጎድጓድ ድምፅ «ና!» ሲል ሰማሁ።
am.B: በጉ ከሰባቱ ማኅተሞች አንዱን ሲፈታ ተመለከትኩ። ከአራቱ ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት አንዱ እንደ ነጎድጓድ ባለ ድምፅ ሲጮኽ ሰማሁ፤ እንዲህም አለ፦ «ና!»
am.R: ከዚያም በጉ ከሰባቱ ማኅተሞች የመጀመሪያውን ሲከፍት አየሁ። ከአራቱ ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት አንዱ እንደ ነጎድጓድ ባለ ድምፅ ሲጮኽ ሰማሁ። እንዲህም አለ፦ «ና!»

hi.L: और मैंने देखा जब मेम्ने ने सात मुहरों में से एक को खोला, और मैंने चारों जीवित प्राणियों में से एक को गर्जन की सी आवाज़ में यह कहते सुना, "आओ!"
hi.B: मैं देखता रहा, और मेम्ने ने सात मुहरों में से एक को तोड़ा। चारों जीवित प्राणियों में से एक ने गर्जन जैसी आवाज़ में पुकारा, और मैंने उसे कहते सुना, "आओ!"
hi.R: फिर मैंने मेम्ने को सात मुहरों में से पहली मुहर खोलते देखा। मैंने चारों जीवित प्राणियों में से एक को गर्जन जैसी आवाज़ में चिल्लाते सुना। उसने कहा, "आओ!"

ru.L: И я видел, когда Агнец снял одну из семи печатей, и услышал одно из четырёх живых существ, говорящее как бы громовым голосом: «Иди!»
ru.B: Я смотрел, как Агнец сломал одну из семи печатей. Одно из четырёх живых существ воскликнуло голосом, подобным грому, и я услышал, как оно говорит: «Иди!»
ru.R: Потом я смотрел, как Агнец сломал первую из семи печатей. Я услышал, как одно из четырёх живых существ закричало голосом, похожим на гром. Оно сказало: «Иди!»

uk.L: І я бачив, коли Агнець відкрив одну із семи печаток, і почув, як одна з чотирьох живих істот казала, наче громовим голосом: «Прийди!»
uk.B: Я дивився, як Агнець зламав одну із семи печаток. Одна з чотирьох живих істот закликала громовим голосом, і я почув, як вона каже: «Прийди!»
uk.R: Потім я дивився, як Ягня відкрило першу із семи печаток. Я почув, як одна з чотирьох живих істот крикнула голосом, подібним до грому. Вона сказала: «Прийди!»

ja.L: また、わたしは、小羊が七つの封印の一つを開かれたとき、[それを]見た。そして、四つの生き物の一つが、雷のような声で「来い！」と言うのを聞いた。
ja.B: わたしは、小羊が七つの封印の一つを開かれるのを見ていた。すると、四つの生き物の一つが雷のような声で叫び、「来い！」と言うのが聞こえた。
ja.R: それから、わたしは、小羊が七つの封印の最初の一つを開かれるのを見ました。四つの生き物の一つが、雷のような声で叫ぶのが聞こえました。その生き物は「来い！」と言いました。

decisions.choice: one of the seven seals: the first
decisions.reason: μίαν "one" is used for "first", as often in the Greek of the New Testament (compare Mark 16:2). The next seals are counted second, third and so on.

decisions.choice: Come! A call to the rider, not to John
alternatives: Come and see, said to John
decisions.reason: The creature calls the horse and rider to come out, and each one goes out (6:2, 4, 5, 8). Some manuscripts add "and see", which makes the call an invitation to John. The SBLGNT reads only "Come". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: four horses: Zechariah's visions
decisions.reason: Zechariah saw horses of different colors sent out to patrol the earth (Zechariah 1:8-11) and four chariots drawn by red, black, white and dappled horses, the four winds of heaven (Zechariah 6:1-8). John's four horsemen draw on these pictures. They also follow the order of the troubles Jesus foretold: war, famine, plague and persecution (Mark 13:7-9; Luke 21:9-12).

decisions.choice: John's visions told in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("je vis", "j’entendis") and the passé composé at Readable ("j’ai vu", "j’ai entendu"); historic presents kept as presents at Literal (6:16 "ils disent")
alternatives: the present throughout, as a vision report
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for Revelation: John tells what he saw as a written narrative, for which French uses the passé simple; Readable uses the passé composé, as spoken French does. Where the Greek tells a past event in the present, Literal keeps it and Balanced narrates it in the passé simple. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: l’Agneau; les quatre êtres vivants; les sceaux (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The style guide's terms for Revelation. "Les quatre animaux", the older French rendering, now suggests beasts; "êtres vivants" keeps the sense of living creatures. "Sceau" is the seal on the scroll; Balanced says the Lamb "brise" it, the natural French verb for breaking a seal, while Literal and Readable keep "ouvrir".

decisions.choice: ¡Ven!
decisions.reason: The call is spoken to each rider, as the meaning decision says, so it is a singular command, the same at every level; nothing is added about seeing.

decisions.choice: "nó" for a living creature
decisions.reason: The living creatures are heavenly beings, not God, and the English calls this one "it"; Vietnamese "nó" is the plain pronoun for a creature, as "chúng" is used for them together (4:6).

decisions.choice: "오너라!" for "Come!" in 6:1-7
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the call as addressed to the rider, not to John (footnoted); "오너라" is a summons, and Korean does not add "and see", which belongs to other manuscripts.

decisions.choice: Venha!
decisions.reason: The call is to the horse and its rider (m2), so it is the ordinary imperative of "você", as the creature speaks to one being, not the "tu" kept for God. Also in 6:3, 5, 7.

decisions.choice: ና! (come!, singular)
decisions.reason: The call is to the rider, who comes out at once, not to John, as the meaning decision says. Amharic must choose a number for the imperative, and the singular "ና" fits one rider and keeps the four calls alike.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; honorific forms for the Lamb
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi (style guide, section 7). The Lamb takes honorific forms ("उन्होंने ... खोली"), as in chapter 5. The same through this chapter.

decisions.choice: "आओ!"
decisions.reason: The call is to each rider (m2), not to John; the living creature commands with the ordinary "तुम" form.

decisions.choice: «Иди!»
decisions.reason: The call is to the rider, not to John (m2), so Russian says "Иди!", sending him out; the longer Synodal form follows a later text.

decisions.choice: «Прийди!» for the creatures' call, at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek is the ordinary "come"; «Прийди!» keeps it, without deciding in the wording whom the call summons, which the meaning decision settles (the rider).

decisions.choice: "開かれた": the seal formula with the respect form for the Lamb
decisions.reason: The Lamb is Christ, so the formula takes the light respect form: "(小羊が)第二の封印を開かれたとき". The same wording is used for every seal, 6:3 to 8:1; Literal leaves the subject unstated, as the Greek does, since the respect form already shows who acts.

decisions.choice: "来い！" (every level)
decisions.reason: The call is to the horse and rider (m2), a short command; the same "来い！" is kept for all four creatures.

source.text: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων τόξον, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στέφανος, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν νικῶν καὶ ἵνα νικήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw, and behold a horse white, and the [one] sitting on it having a bow, and was given to him a crown, and he went out conquering and so that he might conquer.

en.L: And I looked, and look, a white horse, and the one seated on it had a bow, and a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering and to conquer.
en.B: I looked, and I saw a white horse. The one who sat on it carried a bow. A crown was given to him, and out he went, winning victories and set on winning more.
en.R: I looked and saw a white horse. The rider had a bow, and he received a crown. He rode out to win battle after battle.

fr.L: Et je vis, et voici un cheval blanc, et celui qui était assis dessus avait un arc, et une couronne lui fut donnée, et il sortit en vainqueur et pour vaincre.
fr.B: Je regardai, et je vis un cheval blanc. Celui qui le montait portait un arc. On lui donna une couronne, et il partit, remportant des victoires et résolu à en remporter d’autres.
fr.R: J’ai regardé et j’ai vu un cheval blanc. Son cavalier avait un arc, et il a reçu une couronne. Il est parti pour gagner bataille après bataille.

es.L: Y miré, y he aquí un caballo blanco, y el que estaba sentado sobre él tenía un arco, y se le dio una corona, y salió venciendo y para vencer.
es.B: Miré, y vi un caballo blanco. El que lo montaba llevaba un arco. Se le dio una corona, y salió de victoria en victoria, decidido a vencer más aún.
es.R: Miré y vi un caballo blanco. El jinete tenía un arco, y recibió una corona. Salió a ganar una batalla tras otra.

sw.L: Na nilitazama, na tazama, farasi mweupe, na yule aliyeketi juu yake alikuwa na upinde, akapewa taji, akatoka akishinda na ili ashinde.
sw.B: Nilitazama, nikaona farasi mweupe. Yule aliyempanda alibeba upinde. Alipewa taji, naye akatoka, akipata ushindi na akiazimia kushinda zaidi.
sw.R: Nilitazama, nikaona farasi mweupe. Mpanda farasi huyo alikuwa na upinde, naye akapewa taji. Alitoka kwenda kushinda vita moja baada ya nyingine.

vi.L: Và tôi nhìn xem, và kìa, một con ngựa trắng, và người cưỡi nó có một cây cung, và người được ban cho một mão miện, và người đã ra đi như kẻ chiến thắng và để chiến thắng.
vi.B: Tôi nhìn xem, và thấy một con ngựa trắng. Người cưỡi ngựa cầm một cây cung. Người được ban cho một mão miện, và người ra đi, thắng hết trận này đến trận khác và quyết thắng thêm nữa.
vi.R: Tôi nhìn và thấy một con ngựa trắng. Người cưỡi ngựa có một cây cung, và người ấy nhận được một mão miện. Người ấy cưỡi ngựa ra đi để thắng hết trận này đến trận khác.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 보니, 보라, 흰 말이 있었고, 그 위에 탄 자는 활을 가졌으며, 그에게 면류관이 주어졌다. 그는 이기면서 나갔고, 또 이기려고 나갔다.
ko.B: 내가 보니, 흰 말이 있었다. 그 말을 탄 자는 활을 가지고 있었다. 그에게 면류관이 주어졌고, 그는 이기면서 나아갔으며 더 이기려고 나아갔다.
ko.R: 내가 보니, 흰 말이 있었다. 그 말을 탄 자는 활을 가지고 있었고, 면류관을 받았다. 그는 싸울 때마다 이기려고 말을 타고 나갔다.

pt.L: E vi, e eis um cavalo branco, e o que estava montado nele tinha um arco, e foi-lhe dada uma coroa, e ele saiu vencendo e para vencer.
pt.B: Olhei e vi um cavalo branco. Quem o montava tinha um arco. Foi-lhe dada uma coroa, e ele saiu conquistando vitórias e decidido a conquistar ainda mais.
pt.R: Olhei e vi um cavalo branco. O cavaleiro tinha um arco e recebeu uma coroa. Ele saiu para vencer uma batalha atrás da outra.

am.L: አየሁም፤ እነሆም፣ ነጭ ፈረስ [ነበረ]፤ በእርሱም ላይ የተቀመጠው ቀስት ይዞ ነበር፤ አክሊልም ተሰጠው፤ ድል እየነሣና ድል ሊነሣ ወጣ።
am.B: ተመለከትኩ፤ ነጭ ፈረስም አየሁ። በእርሱ ላይ የተቀመጠው ቀስት ይዞ ነበር። አክሊል ተሰጠው፤ ድል እየነሣና ተጨማሪ ድል ለመንሣት ቆርጦ ወጣ።
am.R: ስመለከት ነጭ ፈረስ አየሁ። ጋላቢው ቀስት ይዞ ነበር፤ አክሊልም ተቀበለ። በየጦርነቱ ድል እየነሣ ለመሄድ ወጣ።

hi.L: और मैंने दृष्टि की, और देखो, एक सफ़ेद घोड़ा, और उस पर बैठनेवाले के पास एक धनुष था, और उसे एक मुकुट दिया गया, और वह जय करता हुआ और जय करने को निकला।
hi.B: मैंने दृष्टि की, और एक सफ़ेद घोड़ा देखा। उस पर बैठनेवाला एक धनुष लिए हुए था। उसे एक मुकुट दिया गया, और वह जीत पर जीत पाता हुआ और और जीतने के लिए निकल पड़ा।
hi.R: मैंने देखा तो एक सफ़ेद घोड़ा दिखाई दिया। उसके सवार के पास एक धनुष था, और उसे एक मुकुट मिला। वह एक के बाद एक लड़ाई जीतने के लिए निकल पड़ा।

ru.L: И я взглянул, и вот, конь белый, и сидящий на нём имеет лук, и дан ему был венец, и он вышел побеждающий и чтобы победить.
ru.B: Я взглянул и увидел белого коня. У всадника был лук. Ему дали венец, и он выехал, одерживая победы и стремясь к новым.
ru.R: Я посмотрел и увидел белого коня. У всадника был лук, и ему дали венец. Он поехал побеждать в одной битве за другой.

uk.L: І я глянув, і ось білий кінь, і той, хто сидів на ньому, мав лук, і дано йому вінець, і він вийшов, перемагаючи, і щоб перемогти.
uk.B: Я глянув і побачив білого коня. Вершник на ньому мав лук. Йому дали вінець, і він вирушив, здобуваючи перемоги і прагнучи нових.
uk.R: Я глянув і побачив білого коня. Вершник мав лук, і він отримав вінець. Він поїхав, щоб вигравати одну битву за іншою.

ja.L: そして、わたしは見た。すると見よ、白い馬がいて、それに乗っている者は弓を持っていた。彼には冠が与えられ、彼は勝利を得ながら、さらに勝利を得るために出て行った。
ja.B: わたしが見ていると、そこに白い馬がいた。それに乗っている者は弓を持っていた。彼に冠が与えられ、彼は勝利に勝利を重ねようと出て行った。
ja.R: 見ると、白い馬がいました。それに乗っている者は弓を持っていて、冠を与えられました。彼は次々と戦いに勝とうとして出て行きました。

decisions.choice: the rider on the white horse: conquest, the first of four plagues
alternatives: Christ, or the gospel going out to win the world
a false Christ who imitates him
decisions.reason: Christ rides a white horse in 19:11, and some take this rider to be him or the spread of the gospel. But this rider is one of four sent out by the same call, and the other three bring war, famine and death. He has a bow, not the sword of Christ's mouth (19:15), and he is given his crown. So he most likely stands for conquest and the power of invading armies; the white horse may make him look like a victor, or like Christ. The bow may recall the Parthian mounted archers who threatened Rome's eastern border.

decisions.choice: was given: God permits it
decisions.reason: "Was given" leaves the giver unnamed, but in Revelation it is God who allows the riders to act (compare 6:4, 8; 9:1-5; 13:5-7). Even the forces of war and death act only within the limits he sets.

decisions.choice: conquering (L); winning victories (B); win battle after battle (R)
decisions.reason: νικῶν is the verb rendered "overcome" in the letters. Here its subject wins by force of arms, so the levels use words of military conquest.

decisions.choice: venciendo y para vencer (L); de victoria en victoria, decidido a vencer más aún (B)
decisions.reason: The rider conquers in war, so the verb is the same "vencer" used for the believers' victory, as in the Greek; Readable speaks of battles, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "người cưỡi nó/ngựa", "người"; "được ban cho"
decisions.reason: The rider is conquest, the first of four plagues (m1); "người" names him without honour or contempt, and "được ban cho" keeps the passive that shows God permits it (m2), as through 6:2-8.

decisions.choice: "탄 자" for the riders of 6:2-8; "이기다" for conquering
decisions.reason: The riders are figures of conquest, war, famine and death (meaning decisions), not persons to be honored, so they are "자" with no honorific. The verb is the same as "the one who overcomes" in the letters, and Korean keeps the same verb so the contrast between the two victories can be heard.

decisions.choice: ድል እየነሣና ድል ሊነሣ (conquering and to conquer)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the same verb as for the conquerors of the letters and the Lamb (5:5). Amharic keeps "ድል መንሣት" too, so the reader can see that this rider's victories are a counterfeit of Christ's.

decisions.choice: "दिया गया" kept as a passive
decisions.reason: The passive shows that God permits it (m2), and Hindi keeps it unnamed as the Greek does, through the four riders.

decisions.choice: "すると見よ" (L); no interjection (B, R), for "and behold" in John's narration
decisions.reason: In narration the Greek's "behold" marks something coming into view. Literal keeps the call to attention as "すると見よ", as in 4:1; Balanced and Readable let "わたしが見ると" or "そこに……がいた" carry it. Used wherever "and I saw, and behold" opens a vision in Revelation.

source.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν δευτέραν, ἤκουσα τοῦ δευτέρου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.

es.R: Cuando el Cordero abrió el segundo sello, oí al segundo ser viviente decir: «¡Ven!».

vi.B: Chiên Con gỡ ấn thứ hai, và tôi nghe sinh vật thứ hai nói: "Hãy đến!"

pt.R: Quando o Cordeiro abriu o segundo selo, ouvi o segundo ser vivente dizer: "Venha!"

ru.B: Агнец сломал вторую печать, и я услышал, как второе живое существо сказало: «Иди!»

decisions.choice: the pattern repeats
decisions.reason: Each of the first four seals follows the same pattern: the Lamb opens a seal, one of the living creatures calls "Come!", and a horse and rider go out. See the notes on 6:1.

decisions.choice: the Lamb (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Lamb, who opens every seal (6:1).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
alternatives: a span on the pronouns, as in English
decisions.reason: The English capitalizes pronouns for the Lamb as a reader setting. The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change and the Amharic has no spans; this holds for chapter 6. Balanced and Readable name the Lamb, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And went out another horse fiery-red, and to the [one] sitting on it was given to him to take the peace from the earth, and that one another they will slaughter, and was given to him a sword great.

en.L: And another horse went out, fiery red, and to the one seated on it, it was given to him to take peace from the earth, and that [people] would slaughter one another, and a great sword was given to him.
en.B: Out came another horse, red as fire. The one riding it was permitted to take peace from the earth and to make people slaughter each other, and a great sword was put in his hand.
en.R: Another horse came out. It was bright red. Its rider was allowed to take peace away from the earth, so that people killed each other. He was given a large sword.

fr.L: Et sortit un autre cheval, rouge feu, et à celui qui était assis dessus, il lui fut donné d’ôter la paix de la terre, et que [les gens] s’égorgent les uns les autres, et une grande épée lui fut donnée.
fr.B: Alors sortit un autre cheval, rouge comme le feu. Celui qui le montait reçut le pouvoir d’ôter la paix de la terre et de faire que les gens s’égorgent les uns les autres, et on lui mit en main une grande épée.
fr.R: Un autre cheval est sorti. Il était rouge vif. Son cavalier a reçu la permission d’enlever la paix de la terre, pour que les gens s’entretuent. On lui a donné une grande épée.

es.L: Y salió otro caballo, rojo como el fuego, y al que estaba sentado sobre él se le concedió quitar la paz de la tierra, y que [la gente] se degollara unos a otros, y se le dio una gran espada.

es.R: Salió otro caballo. Era de un rojo intenso. A su jinete se le permitió quitar la paz de la tierra, para que la gente se matara unos a otros. Se le dio una espada grande.

ko.L: 그러자 붉은 다른 말이 나왔다. 그 위에 탄 자에게 땅에서 평화를 없애고 사람들이 서로 죽이게 하는 일이 허락되었다. 그리고 그에게 큰 칼이 주어졌다.

pt.L: E saiu outro cavalo, vermelho como fogo, e ao que estava montado nele foi-lhe dado tirar a paz da terra, e que [as pessoas] se matassem umas às outras, e foi-lhe dada uma grande espada.

am.L: ሌላም እንደ እሳት ቀይ የሆነ ፈረስ ወጣ፤ በእርሱም ላይ ለተቀመጠው ሰላምን ከምድር እንዲወስድ፣ [ሰዎችም] እርስ በርሳቸው እንዲተራረዱ ተሰጠው፤ ታላቅ ሰይፍም ተሰጠው።

hi.L: और एक दूसरा घोड़ा निकला, आग जैसा लाल, और उस पर बैठनेवाले को यह दिया गया कि पृथ्वी पर से शान्ति उठा ले, और कि [लोग] एक दूसरे का वध करें, और उसे एक बड़ी तलवार दी गई।

ru.L: И вышел другой конь, огненно-рыжий, и сидящему на нём дано было взять мир с земли, и чтобы [люди] убивали друг друга, и дан ему был большой меч.

uk.R: Вийшов ще один кінь. Він був яскраво-червоний. Його вершникові дозволили забрати мир із землі, щоб люди вбивали одне одного. Йому дали великий меч.

ja.L: すると、別の火のように赤い馬が出て来た。それに乗っている者には、地上から平和を取り去り、[人々が]互いに殺し合うようにすることが与えられた。また、彼には大きな剣が与えられた。

ja.R: すると、別の馬が出て来ました。真っ赤な馬でした。それに乗っている者は、地上から平和を取り去ることを許されました。それで人々は互いに殺し合いました。彼には大きな剣が与えられました。

decisions.choice: the red horse: war and bloodshed
decisions.reason: Red is the color of fire and blood. The rider takes away peace, so that people slaughter one another, which may mean civil strife as well as war between nations. σφάξουσιν is the word used of the slaughtered Lamb (5:6, 9): people now do to one another what was done to him.

decisions.choice: was given: God permits it
decisions.reason: "Was given" leaves the giver unnamed, but in Revelation it is God who allows the riders to act (compare 6:4, 8; 9:1-5; 13:5-7). Even the forces of war and death act only within the limits he sets.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "they will slaughter one another". Every level supplies who: the people of the earth.

decisions.choice: "hòa bình" for the peace taken from the earth; "người ta" with no gender span
decisions.reason: This is peace between peoples, the absence of war (m1), so Vietnamese says "hòa bình"; "bình an", the key term, stays for God's peace (1:4). "Người ta" already includes everyone.

decisions.choice: matassem (L, B); matar (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the slaughtered Lamb (m1); Portuguese "sacrificar", used for the Lamb (5:6), cannot be said of people killing each other in war, so every level uses the plain "matar", as the English Readable says "killed".

decisions.choice: "……することが与えられた" (L); "許された" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The unnamed giver is God, who permits the riders to act (m2). Literal keeps the Greek's "was given"; Balanced and Readable say "was allowed", as the English does. Used for this passive through chapters 6-9.

decisions.choice: "殺し合う" (every level)
decisions.reason: "屠り合う" would keep the link with the slaughtered Lamb (m1) but is not natural Japanese; the note carries the link.

source.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξε τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τρίτην, ἤκουσα τοῦ τρίτου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.

records.literal_gloss: And when he opened the seal the third, I heard the third living creature saying: Come.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, "Come!"
en.B: The Lamb broke the third seal, and I heard the third living creature say, "Come!"
en.R: When the Lamb opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, "Come!"

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ouvrit le troisième sceau, j’entendis le troisième être vivant dire : « Viens ! »
fr.B: L’Agneau brisa le troisième sceau, et j’entendis le troisième être vivant dire : « Viens ! »
fr.R: Quand l’Agneau a ouvert le troisième sceau, j’ai entendu le troisième être vivant dire : « Viens ! »

es.L: Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} abrió el tercer sello, oí al tercer ser viviente que decía: «¡Ven!».
es.B: El Cordero rompió el tercer sello, y oí al tercer ser viviente decir: «¡Ven!».
es.R: Cuando el Cordero abrió el tercer sello, oí al tercer ser viviente decir: «¡Ven!».

sw.L: Na alipoufungua muhuri wa tatu, nilimsikia kiumbe hai wa tatu akisema, "Njoo!"
sw.B: Mwanakondoo aliuvunja muhuri wa tatu, nikamsikia kiumbe hai wa tatu akisema, "Njoo!"
sw.R: Mwanakondoo alipoufungua muhuri wa tatu, nilimsikia kiumbe hai wa tatu akisema, "Njoo!"

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mở ấn thứ ba, tôi nghe sinh vật thứ ba nói: "Hãy đến!"
vi.B: Chiên Con gỡ ấn thứ ba, và tôi nghe sinh vật thứ ba nói: "Hãy đến!"
vi.R: Khi Chiên Con mở ấn thứ ba, tôi nghe sinh vật thứ ba nói: "Hãy đến!"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 셋째 봉인을 떼실 때에, 나는 셋째 생물이 "오너라!" 하고 말하는 것을 들었다.
ko.B: 어린양이 셋째 봉인을 떼셨을 때, 나는 셋째 생물이 "오너라!" 하고 말하는 것을 들었다.
ko.R: 어린양이 셋째 봉인을 떼셨을 때, 나는 셋째 생물이 "오너라!" 하고 말하는 것을 들었다.

pt.L: E quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} abriu o terceiro selo, ouvi o terceiro ser vivente dizendo: "Venha!"
pt.B: O Cordeiro rompeu o terceiro selo, e ouvi o terceiro ser vivente dizer: "Venha!"
pt.R: Quando o Cordeiro abriu o terceiro selo, ouvi o terceiro ser vivente dizer: "Venha!"

am.L: ሦስተኛውንም ማኅተም በከፈተ ጊዜ ሦስተኛው ሕያው ፍጡር «ና!» ሲል ሰማሁ።
am.B: በጉ ሦስተኛውን ማኅተም ሲፈታ ሦስተኛው ሕያው ፍጡር «ና!» ሲል ሰማሁ።
am.R: በጉ ሦስተኛውን ማኅተም ሲከፍት ሦስተኛው ሕያው ፍጡር «ና!» ሲል ሰማሁ።

hi.L: और जब उन्होंने तीसरी मुहर खोली, तो मैंने तीसरे जीवित प्राणी को यह कहते सुना, "आओ!"
hi.B: मेम्ने ने तीसरी मुहर तोड़ी, और मैंने तीसरे जीवित प्राणी को कहते सुना, "आओ!"
hi.R: जब मेम्ने ने तीसरी मुहर खोली, तो मैंने तीसरे जीवित प्राणी को कहते सुना, "आओ!"

ru.L: И когда {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} снял третью печать, я услышал третье живое существо, говорящее: «Иди!»
ru.B: Агнец сломал третью печать, и я услышал, как третье живое существо сказало: «Иди!»
ru.R: Когда Агнец сломал третью печать, я услышал, как третье живое существо сказало: «Иди!»

uk.L: І коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} відкрив третю печатку, я почув, як третя жива істота казала: «Прийди!»
uk.B: Агнець зламав третю печатку, і я почув, як третя жива істота сказала: «Прийди!»
uk.R: Коли Ягня відкрило третю печатку, я почув, як третя жива істота сказала: «Прийди!»

ja.L: そして、第三の封印を開かれたとき、わたしは第三の生き物が「来い！」と言うのを聞いた。
ja.B: 小羊が第三の封印を開かれたとき、わたしは第三の生き物が「来い！」と言うのを聞いた。
ja.R: 小羊が第三の封印を開かれたとき、第三の生き物が「来い！」と言うのが聞こえました。

decisions.choice: the pattern repeats
decisions.reason: Each of the first four seals follows the same pattern: the Lamb opens a seal, one of the living creatures calls "Come!", and a horse and rider go out. See the notes on 6:1.

decisions.choice: the Lamb (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Lamb, who opens every seal (6:1).

source.text: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος μέλας, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων ζυγὸν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw, and behold a horse black, and the [one] sitting on it having a balance in the hand of him.

en.L: And I looked, and look, a black horse, and the one seated on it had a pair of scales in his hand.
en.B: I looked, and there was a black horse, and the one who sat on it had a balance in his hand.
en.R: I looked and saw a black horse. Its rider was holding scales for weighing food.

fr.L: Et je vis, et voici un cheval noir, et celui qui était assis dessus avait une balance dans sa main.
fr.B: Je regardai, et voici un cheval noir ; celui qui le montait tenait une balance à la main.
fr.R: J’ai regardé et j’ai vu un cheval noir. Son cavalier tenait une balance pour peser la nourriture.

es.L: Y miré, y he aquí un caballo negro, y el que estaba sentado sobre él tenía una balanza en su mano.
es.B: Miré, y había un caballo negro, y el que lo montaba tenía una balanza en la mano.
es.R: Miré y vi un caballo negro. Su jinete tenía en la mano una balanza para pesar alimentos.

sw.L: Na nilitazama, na tazama, farasi mweusi, na yule aliyeketi juu yake alikuwa na mizani mkononi mwake.
sw.B: Nilitazama, na pale palikuwa na farasi mweusi, na yule aliyempanda alikuwa na mizani mkononi mwake.
sw.R: Nilitazama, nikaona farasi mweusi. Mpanda farasi wake alikuwa ameshika mizani ya kupimia chakula.

vi.L: Và tôi nhìn xem, và kìa, một con ngựa đen, và người cưỡi nó cầm một cái cân trong tay.
vi.B: Tôi nhìn xem, và thấy một con ngựa đen. Người cưỡi ngựa cầm một cái cân trong tay.
vi.R: Tôi nhìn và thấy một con ngựa đen. Người cưỡi ngựa cầm một cái cân để cân lương thực.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 보니, 보라, 검은 말이 있었고, 그 위에 탄 자는 손에 저울을 가지고 있었다.
ko.B: 내가 보니, 검은 말이 있었고, 그 말을 탄 자는 손에 저울을 들고 있었다.
ko.R: 내가 보니, 검은 말이 있었다. 그 말을 탄 자는 곡식을 다는 저울을 들고 있었다.

pt.L: E vi, e eis um cavalo preto, e o que estava montado nele tinha uma balança na sua mão.
pt.B: Olhei, e lá estava um cavalo preto, e quem o montava tinha uma balança na mão.
pt.R: Olhei e vi um cavalo preto. O seu cavaleiro segurava uma balança para pesar comida.

am.L: አየሁም፤ እነሆም፣ ጥቁር ፈረስ [ነበረ]፤ በእርሱም ላይ የተቀመጠው በእጁ ሚዛን ይዞ ነበር።
am.B: ተመለከትኩ፤ ጥቁር ፈረስም ነበረ፤ በእርሱ ላይ የተቀመጠው በእጁ ሚዛን ይዞ ነበር።
am.R: ስመለከት ጥቁር ፈረስ አየሁ። ጋላቢው እህል የሚመዝንበት ሚዛን ይዞ ነበር።

hi.L: और मैंने दृष्टि की, और देखो, एक काला घोड़ा, और उस पर बैठनेवाले के हाथ में एक तराज़ू था।
hi.B: मैंने दृष्टि की, और वहाँ एक काला घोड़ा था, और उस पर बैठनेवाले के हाथ में एक तराज़ू था।
hi.R: मैंने देखा तो एक काला घोड़ा दिखाई दिया। उसका सवार अनाज तौलने का तराज़ू लिए हुए था।

ru.L: И я взглянул, и вот, конь чёрный, и сидящий на нём имеет весы в своей руке.
ru.B: Я взглянул, и вот был чёрный конь, а у всадника в руке были весы.
ru.R: Я посмотрел и увидел чёрного коня. Всадник держал весы, чтобы взвешивать еду.

uk.L: І я глянув, і ось чорний кінь, і той, хто сидів на ньому, мав терези у своїй руці.
uk.B: Я глянув, і ось чорний кінь, а вершник на ньому тримав у руці терези.
uk.R: Я глянув і побачив чорного коня. Його вершник тримав терези, щоб зважувати їжу.

ja.L: そして、わたしは見た。すると見よ、黒い馬がいて、それに乗っている者は手に秤を持っていた。
ja.B: わたしが見ていると、そこに黒い馬がいた。それに乗っている者は手に天秤を持っていた。
ja.R: 見ると、黒い馬がいました。それに乗っている者は、食べ物を量るはかりを手に持っていました。

decisions.choice: a balance: scales for weighing food, a sign of scarcity
decisions.reason: ζυγὸν is a beam balance used in the market. When food was scarce it was weighed out carefully (compare Ezekiel 4:16, "they shall eat bread by weight and with anxiety"). The black horse brings famine.

decisions.choice: scales for weighing food (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the scales were for (m1).

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγουσαν· Χοῖνιξ σίτου δηναρίου, καὶ τρεῖς χοίνικες κριθῶν δηναρίου· καὶ τὸ ἔλαιον καὶ τὸν οἶνον μὴ ἀδικήσῃς.

records.literal_gloss: And I heard as a voice in [the] middle of the four living creatures saying: A choenix of wheat of a denarius, and three choenixes of barley of a denarius; and the oil and the wine not harm.

en.L: And I heard [something] like a voice in [the] middle of the four living creatures, saying, "A choenix of wheat for a denarius, and three choenixes of barley for a denarius, and do not harm the oil and the wine."
en.B: And I heard what sounded like a voice among the four living creatures, saying: "A {{units:quart|choenix}} of wheat for {{units:a day's wages|a denarius}}, and three {{units:quarts|choenixes}} of barley for {{units:a day's wages|a denarius}}, but do not damage the olive oil and the wine!"
en.R: Then I heard something like a voice coming from among the four living creatures. It said, "Only one {{units:quart|choenix}} of wheat for {{units:a whole day's pay|a denarius}}, or three {{units:quarts|choenixes}} of barley for {{units:a whole day's pay|a denarius}}! But do not harm the olive oil and the wine."

fr.L: Et j’entendis comme une voix au milieu des quatre êtres vivants, qui disait : « Une chénice de blé pour un denier, et trois chénices d’orge pour un denier ; et n’abîme pas l’huile et le vin. »
fr.B: J’entendis alors comme une voix au milieu des quatre êtres vivants, qui disait : « {{units:Un litre|Une chénice}} de blé pour {{units:une journée de salaire|un denier}}, et {{units:trois litres|trois chénices}} d’orge pour {{units:une journée de salaire|un denier}} ; mais n’abîme pas l’huile d’olive et le vin ! »
fr.R: Ensuite, j’ai entendu comme une voix qui venait du milieu des quatre êtres vivants. Elle disait : « {{units:Un seul litre|Une seule chénice}} de blé pour {{units:une journée entière de salaire|un denier}}, ou {{units:trois litres|trois chénices}} d’orge pour {{units:une journée entière de salaire|un denier}} ! Mais ne touche pas à l’huile d’olive ni au vin. »

es.L: Y oí como una voz en medio de los cuatro seres vivientes, que decía: «Una quénice de trigo por un denario, y tres quénices de cebada por un denario; y no dañes el aceite y el vino».
es.B: Y oí lo que parecía una voz en medio de los cuatro seres vivientes, que decía: «{{units:Un litro|Una quénice}} de trigo por {{units:el salario de un día|un denario}}, y tres {{units:litros|quénices}} de cebada por {{units:el salario de un día|un denario}}, ¡pero no dañes el aceite de oliva ni el vino!».
es.R: Entonces oí algo como una voz que venía de en medio de los cuatro seres vivientes. Decía: «¡Solo {{units:un litro|una quénice}} de trigo por {{units:el salario de todo un día|un denario}}, o tres {{units:litros|quénices}} de cebada por {{units:el salario de todo un día|un denario}}! Pero no dañes el aceite de oliva ni el vino».

sw.L: Na nilisikia [kitu] kama sauti katikati ya wale viumbe hai wanne, ikisema, "Koiniksi moja ya ngano kwa dinari moja, na koiniksi tatu za shayiri kwa dinari moja, wala usiyadhuru mafuta na divai."
sw.B: Kisha nikasikia kile kilichosikika kama sauti katikati ya viumbe hai wanne, ikisema: "{{units:Lita moja|Koiniksi moja}} ya ngano kwa {{units:mshahara wa siku moja|dinari moja}}, na {{units:lita tatu|koiniksi tatu}} za shayiri kwa {{units:mshahara wa siku moja|dinari moja}}, lakini usiyadhuru mafuta ya zeituni wala divai!"
sw.R: Kisha nikasikia kitu kama sauti ikitoka katikati ya viumbe hai wanne. Ilisema, "Ni {{units:lita moja tu|koiniksi moja tu}} ya ngano kwa {{units:mshahara wa siku nzima|dinari moja}}, au {{units:lita tatu|koiniksi tatu}} za shayiri kwa {{units:mshahara wa siku nzima|dinari moja}}! Lakini usiyadhuru mafuta ya zeituni wala divai."

vi.L: Và tôi nghe như có tiếng ở giữa bốn sinh vật nói: "Một xô-ních lúa mì giá một đơ-ni-ê, và ba xô-ních lúa mạch giá một đơ-ni-ê; còn dầu và rượu thì đừng làm hại."
vi.B: Và tôi nghe có tiếng như tiếng nói ở giữa bốn sinh vật: "{{units:Một lít|Một xô-ních}} lúa mì giá {{units:một ngày công|một đơ-ni-ê}}, và {{units:ba lít|ba xô-ních}} lúa mạch giá {{units:một ngày công|một đơ-ni-ê}}; nhưng đừng làm hại dầu ô-liu và rượu nho!"
vi.R: Rồi tôi nghe có tiếng như tiếng nói từ giữa bốn sinh vật. Tiếng ấy nói: "Chỉ {{units:một lít|một xô-ních}} lúa mì mà giá bằng {{units:tiền công cả một ngày|một đơ-ni-ê}}, hay {{units:ba lít|ba xô-ních}} lúa mạch mà giá bằng {{units:tiền công cả một ngày|một đơ-ni-ê}}! Nhưng đừng làm hại dầu ô-liu và rượu nho."

ko.L: 그리고 나는 네 생물 한가운데서 나는 듯한 음성이 이렇게 말하는 것을 들었다. "한 데나리온에 밀 한 코이닉스요, 한 데나리온에 보리 세 코이닉스다. 그리고 기름과 포도주는 해치지 마라."
ko.B: 그리고 나는 네 생물 사이에서 나는 음성 같은 것을 들었다. "{{units:하루 품삯|한 데나리온}}에 밀 {{units:1리터|한 코이닉스}}, {{units:하루 품삯|한 데나리온}}에 보리 {{units:3리터|세 코이닉스}}다! 그러나 올리브기름과 포도주는 해치지 마라!"
ko.R: 그때 나는 네 생물 사이에서 나오는 음성 같은 것을 들었다. "{{units:하루 종일 일한 품삯|한 데나리온}}으로 겨우 밀 {{units:1리터|한 코이닉스}}를 산다! 또는 보리 {{units:3리터|세 코이닉스}}를 산다! 그러나 올리브기름과 포도주는 해치지 마라."

pt.L: E ouvi como [que] uma voz no meio dos quatro seres viventes, dizendo: "Uma quênice de trigo por um denário, e três quênices de cevada por um denário, e não danifique o azeite e o vinho."
pt.B: E ouvi algo como uma voz no meio dos quatro seres viventes, que dizia: "{{units:Um litro|Uma quênice}} de trigo por {{units:um dia de salário|um denário}}, e {{units:três litros|três quênices}} de cevada por {{units:um dia de salário|um denário}}, mas não estrague o azeite e o vinho!"
pt.R: Então ouvi algo parecido com uma voz que vinha do meio dos quatro seres viventes. Ela disse: "Só {{units:um litro|uma quênice}} de trigo pelo {{units:salário de um dia inteiro|preço de um denário}}, ou {{units:três litros|três quênices}} de cevada pelo {{units:salário de um dia inteiro|preço de um denário}}! Mas não estrague o azeite e o vinho."

am.L: በአራቱም ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት መካከል እንደ ድምፅ ያለ [ነገር] እንዲህ ሲል ሰማሁ፦ «አንድ ኮይኒክስ ስንዴ በአንድ ዲናር፣ ሦስት ኮይኒክስ ገብስም በአንድ ዲናር፤ ዘይቱንና የወይን ጠጁን ግን አትጉዳ።»

decisions.choice: famine prices: a day's wage for a day's food
decisions.reason: A denarius was a laborer's pay for a day (Matthew 20:2). A choenix, a little over a quart, was about the grain one person ate in a day. The prices are many times the usual, so that a day's work buys bread for the worker alone, or cheaper barley for a small family. It describes severe scarcity, not starvation.

decisions.choice: spare the oil and the wine: a famine that is limited
alternatives: the rich keep their luxuries while the poor go hungry
decisions.reason: Olive trees and vines have deep roots and survive a drought that ruins a grain harvest. The command limits the famine: it is severe but not total. Some take oil and wine as luxuries, so that the famine hurts the poor most. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: something like a voice among the creatures
decisions.reason: The voice comes from the center of the four living creatures, where the throne and the Lamb are (4:6; 5:6). It is most likely the voice of God or the Lamb, setting limits to the judgment.

decisions.choice: units: quart, a day's wages
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek units. Balanced and Readable give modern equivalents, with "choenix" and "denarius" as the alternatives, so the reader can see what the prices meant (m1).

decisions.choice: units: "un litre", "trois litres" and "une journée de salaire" by default, "chénice" and "denier" as the alternatives (B, R); Literal "une chénice", "un denier"
alternatives: un denier and une chénice at every level
decisions.reason: French uses metric measures, so the default differs from the English "quart": a choenix held a little more than a litre, about one person's daily ration of grain. "Chénice" is the traditional French name of the measure and "denier" of the coin, a labourer's daily wage, so the alternatives and Literal keep them. The units span holds the article, which changes with the noun ("un litre", "une chénice").

decisions.choice: {{units:un litro|una quénice}}; {{units:el salario de un día|un denario}}
decisions.reason: A choenix held a little over a liter of grain, so the metric default is "litro", the measure Spanish readers use; the coin is given as a day's wage, as in John 6:7 and 12:5. Literal keeps the original names "quénice" and "denario" with no span, as the English Literal does. The article stays inside the span, since "quénice" is feminine and "litro" masculine.

decisions.choice: {{units:lita moja|koiniksi moja}}; {{units:mshahara wa siku moja|dinari moja}}
decisions.reason: As the Swahili style guide sets for units: metric by default (a choenix held a little over a litre of grain), with the original measure as the alternative, where the English default is the US quart. The coin is given as a day's wage, as John 6:7 and 12:5. Literal keeps "koiniksi" and "dinari" with no span, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: {{units:một lít|một xô-ních}} and {{units:một ngày công|một đơ-ni-ê}} (B, R); the original measures at Literal
decisions.reason: The style guide sets metric by default, with the original unit as the alternative, where the English converts to US units: a choenix was about a litre of grain, a day's ration. The denarius is given as a day's wage, as in the Vietnamese Matthew (20:2), since that is the point of the famine price (m1). Literal keeps the Greek units, "xô-ních" in the hyphenated form used for names and "đơ-ni-ê" as in the Gospels.

decisions.choice: {{units:하루 품삯|한 데나리온}} (B), {{units:하루 종일 일한 품삯|한 데나리온}} (R); {{units:1리터|한 코이닉스}}, {{units:3리터|세 코이닉스}} (B, R); Literal keeps "데나리온" and "코이닉스"
alternatives: US quarts, as in the English
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Gospels (Matthew 20:2), money is given in wages by default with the coin as the alternative; the dry measure is metric by default (Korean style guide, section 7), unlike the English quarts. A choenix was a little over a liter. The particles after each span fit both forms.

decisions.choice: um litro, um dia de salário (B, R); quênice, denário (L)
decisions.reason: As style section 7: Balanced and Readable give the metric measure by default, "litro" (a choenix was a little over a litre), and a day's wages, with the Greek units as the alternative, where the English default is US quarts. "Quênice" is the Portuguese form of the Greek measure; few readers know it, which is why Literal alone keeps it without a setting, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: units setting: አንድ ሊትር ያህል (about a liter) or አንድ ኮይኒክስ (a choenix); በአንድ ቀን ደመወዝ (for a day's wages, B), በሙሉ ቀን ደመወዝ (R), or በአንድ ዲናር (for a denarius)
alternatives: the US quart, as in the English
decisions.reason: As in French and Swahili, Amharic gives a measure in metric units by default: a choenix held a little over a liter of grain, a day's food for one person. The coin has no metric form, so the default gives its value, a day's wages, as Matthew does; the original choenix and denarius are the alternatives, and Literal keeps them.

decisions.choice: "{{units:लगभग एक लीटर|एक खोइनिक्स}}"; "{{units:एक दिन की मज़दूरी|एक दीनार}}"
decisions.reason: The Hindi units setting is metric by default with the original unit as the alternative (style guide, section 7); a choenix was a little over a litre, about one person's daily ration of grain. The coin has no metric form, so the default gives its value in wages, as the English does (m1). Literal keeps the Greek measure and coin.

decisions.choice: "दाखरस" (wine)
decisions.reason: The established Bible word for wine, kept through the book.

decisions.choice: {{units:литр|хиникс}}; {{units:дневной заработок|денарий}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Russian units setting is metric by default, so the choenix (a little over a litre) is "литр" where the English has "quart"; the coin is a day's wages by default, as in Matthew 20:2, with "денарий" as the alternative. Literal keeps the Greek units.

decisions.choice: {{units:літр|хінікс}}: the measure in litres by default, the Greek measure as the alternative; Literal keeps "хінікс"
alternatives: the English default, a US quart
decisions.reason: Ukrainian readers measure in litres, so the metric figure is the default, as the Ukrainian style guide sets for the units setting; a choenix is a little over a litre. The same holds for the other measures in the book (14:20; 16:21; 21:16-17).

decisions.choice: {{units:денний заробіток|динарій}} for the coin, as the English does
decisions.reason: A coin has no metric form; the default gives its value in wages, as the meaning decision explains (a day's wage for a day's food).

decisions.choice: {{units:約1リットル|一コイニクス}}, {{units:一日分の賃金|一デナリオン}} (B, R); the Greek units in Literal
decisions.reason: The Japanese units setting is metric: a choenix is a little over a liter. The coin is given as a day's wages, as in English, with the coin as the alternative. Literal keeps "コイニクス" and "デナリオン".
